headline: Rivian spinoff Also starts shipping e-bikes after months of delays
summary: Also's $4,500 TM-B e-bike, originally slated for a Spring 2026 delivery, will now ship to customers between next week and September.
details: Rivian spinoff Also is finally set to deliver its first e-bikes to customers next week, following significant delays attributed to unspecified supply chain issues. The Launch Edition of the TM-B e-bike, priced at $4,500, has begun shipping from the manufacturer to Also's U.S. warehouse, with all Launch Edition bikes expected to be delivered by September.

Also originated as a project within Rivian in 2022, with early design input from Jony Ive's firm LoveFrom. Rivian spun Also out as an independent company in March 2025, securing $105 million in funding. The startup unveiled the TM-B e-bike in October 2025, initially targeting a Spring 2026 delivery.

The company cited "stress on global supply chains" and a "rapid, industry-wide spike in demand for raw materials and electronic components" as the primary reasons for the delay. Also stated that its teams are working diligently to mitigate these constraints without compromising safety or quality, though specific components causing the holdup were not disclosed.

Despite the e-bike delays, Also has ambitious plans, referring to itself as a "vehicle" company. Future projects include four-wheel pedal-assist cargo vehicles for Amazon and an autonomous delivery vehicle for DoorDash.

The delay has caused frustration among some customers, with comments on Reddit expressing disappointment over "lack of communication and actual miscommunication/lies from Also regarding shipment timelines." Some customers have reportedly canceled their reservations due to the repeated postponements.
